explained.headline: South Africans vote in local elections amid ANC struggles

happened.text: South Africans began voting on Wednesday in municipal elections to decide who leads the country's local councils and major cities.
The vote takes place amid deep discontent over power cuts, water outages and crumbling infrastructure.
Polls suggested the governing party could receive less than a third of the vote.

background.text: The party lost its parliamentary majority in 2024, leading to a national coalition government.
Opposition forces include the liberal Democratic Alliance and the leftwing uMkhonto weSizwe party led by former president Jacob Zuma.

matters.text: Further declines in popularity could result in many South African cities being run by unstable coalition governments.
Analysts state that high turnover in fragile municipal coalitions is a major reason for poor service delivery.

uncertain.text: The electoral commission has up to a week to announce the final results.
Parties have two weeks following the announcement of results to form councils and elect mayors.

terms.definition: A large urban area in South Africa with a single municipal authority.

removed.text: The African National Congress, led to power in 1994 by Nelson Mandela at the end of apartheid, has governed South Africa ever since.
why: The evidence does not confirm the ANC has governed South Africa without interruption since 1994.

explained.headline: Democrats win US midterms and seize control of Congress

happened.text: Democrats have taken control of the United States House of Representatives and Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections.
The Democratic majority gives the party the chairmanships of all congressional committees, enabling them to launch investigations and subpoena witnesses.
The shift in legislative control could impact policies ranging from military funding and trade tariffs to immigration and foreign aid.

background.text: The Republican Party previously secured both the presidency and majorities in both chambers of Congress during the 2024 elections.
Donald Trump, the United States president, embarked on a war with Israel against Iran in February without congressional authorisation.
Voter frustration regarding inflation and the rising cost of fuel and groceries contributed heavily to the Republican defeat.

matters.text: James Boys, research fellow at the Centre on US Politics at University College London, stated that Donald Trump may feel unleashed to act with impunity on the world stage.
Michael O'Hanlon, director of research for foreign policy at the Brookings Institution, said Congress could perhaps prevent a major escalation in the Iran conflict by refusing to fund it.

uncertain.text: James Boys noted that whether the government must return already collected tariff money, and exactly how much, remains in dispute before United States courts.
It remains questionable whether a Democratic-controlled Congress could reactivate the closed United States Agency for International Development against the president's wishes.

terms.definition: A tax imposed by a government on imported goods from other countries.
The constitutional right of a president to reject a decision or proposal passed by a lawmaking body.

removed.text: Brandon Conradis, a former journalist and now an editor at Bloomberg Government, said that Democrats can push legislation to provide more aid to Ukraine.
Analysts remain divided on whether cutting off military funding for the war on Iran is practically straightforward given deployed troops.

explained.headline: Ukraine Strikes Russia as Delegations Head to White House

happened.text: Ukrainian drone strikes killed three people in Russia's Belgorod region and hit energy infrastructure, while Russian attacks damaged power facilities across nine regions in Ukraine.
A Ukrainian drone attack also started a fire at a major Ozon distribution facility in the Republic of Adygea.
Russian and Ukrainian delegations are due to meet at the White House following a six-day local ceasefire in Oleshky that enabled civilian evacuations.

background.text: The conflict between Russia and Ukraine escalated significantly after Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy subsequently awarded Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga for her humanitarian support and role in the ceasefire.

matters.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that the Kremlin hopes United States President Donald Trump will continue his peacemaking efforts following the recent midterms.
Democratic control of the legislature in January is expected to bring a more vocal pro-Kyiv majority in Congress that could pressure the US president to change tack.
Representative officials note that important discussions on postwar security agreements and de-escalation are scheduled for upcoming trilateral meetings.

uncertain.text: It remains unclarified how many households were affected by the temporary outage schedules enforced in Crimea after the energy strikes.
Neither the Russian nor Ukrainian sides elaborated on the exact nature or extent of Melania Trump's involvement in brokering the ceasefire.
The White House has not yet shared specific details regarding what the upcoming White House delegation event will entail.

terms.definition: An official appointed to represent the interests of the public by investigating and addressing grievances against public authorities.
An auxiliary power station where electrical voltage is transformed for transmission or distribution.

removed.text: The United States First Lady Melania Trump independently initiated engagement between the two warring nations to secure the Oleshky ceasefire.
why: The claim states the White House's assertion as an objective fact without attribution.
